effective_to_week.description: Null means current. Derived from the NEXT revision's effective_from_week and never stored on both sides -- see revisions.py.

head_coach_id.description: A name-derived surrogate. There is no coach-identity service; player-identity is authoritative for players only. head_coach_name is published beside it so a consumer can tell a re-spelling from a real change.

offensive_coordinator_id.description: Null by necessity. No free feed names coordinators; the spec's own candidate is scraping Pro Football Reference staff pages. See null_field_reason.

defensive_coordinator_id.description: Null by necessity, same reason as offensive_coordinator_id.

play_caller_id.description: Populated ONLY from the curated register in play_callers.py, which ships empty. Never defaulted to the head coach -- that default is right often enough to look correct and wrong exactly when a play-calling handoff happens, which is the event this collector exists to detect.

play_caller_source.description: The evidence behind the assertion. Required non-empty on every register entry, so a populated play_caller_id always carries its provenance onto the wire.

play_caller_missing_reason.description: Exactly one of this and play_caller_id is non-null. 'expired' and 'unknown' are distinct because they imply different work: a re-check versus a first look.

change_event.description: DEVIATION: 'unclassified' is added to the spec's enum. The feed states that the head coach changed and nothing about why; picking a cause would be fabrication and 'none' would be false. See revisions.py.

change_reported_at.description: Null by necessity. No feed carries a staff-change publication instant, and inferring one from our own fetch time would state an observation as an announcement.

games_sampled.description: Games inside THIS revision's window only. Guard 1 refuses a row whose games_sampled exceeds the revision's week span -- a team plays at most one game a week.

sampled_weeks.description: Every week folded into these rates. Published so a consumer can verify guard 1 rather than trust it: every entry must lie inside [effective_from_week, effective_to_week].

pass_rate_over_expected.description: PERCENTAGE POINTS, not a share: nflfastR's pass_oe is (pass - xpass) * 100. That is also what makes changepoint.py's 8.0 threshold the spec's 'eight points' with no conversion.

personnel_rates.description: Shares of classified offensive snaps. They do NOT sum to 1.0: 10 and 20 personnel are real and belong in no named bucket. Null when the participation feed was unavailable -- 'no evidence', never 'zero'.

fourth_down_go_rate_over_expected.description: Null by necessity. nflfastR publishes wp and vegas_wp but no fourth-down recommendation; a baseline invented here would look like the well-known public one and not be it.

changepoint_unexplained.description: Guard 2. NULL means the detector is disabled and this row was NOT checked -- see null_field_reason and changepoint.py, which carries the five seasons of measurement: a weekly-PROE mean-shift test fires on 65% of real team-seasons against 55% of week-shuffled ones, and the oracle test cannot separate a real head-coach change from an arbitrary week (mean |shift| 4.83 vs 4.01 points, p = 0.18 at n = 12). False would assert 'checked and clean', which this collector cannot support. True (unreachable today) means the series shifted with no corresponding staff revision, so the rates on BOTH sides are suspect -- surfaced, not corrected.

changepoint_shift.description: PROE points, signed. Positive means the offense became more pass-happy than expected after the shift.

changepoint_p_value.description: Against the team's OWN week-permuted null, so it adapts to that team's volatility rather than to a league-wide constant. Never 0: the observed value is included in its own reference set, which is what keeps the test exact.

degraded_upstreams.description: Which optional feeds were missing on the pass that produced this row, so a null rate is attributable rather than merely absent.

null_field_reason.comment: changepoint_unexplained appears here only while guard 2 is disabled; once it carries a real boolean it needs no excuse.
